Why is this marked WIP?  The dependency is met due to the common topic.  Marking WIP means this isn't likely to be reviewed.
I don't think there is a way we can make this work.  See my comments about Redfish message versions.

This doesn't work because you still don't know which arguments are intended to be sent via Redfish and which ones are not.  In the sdbusplus YAML format there is a "primary" field that identifies which ones are intended to be sent via Redfish.
I updated the sdbusplus to only get the primary Redfish arguments.
Can we just skip all this _SOURCE stuff in this path?  You added it in sdbusplus for some reason and then you have to avoid it here.  Seems like a lot of extra work.
I removed checking `_SOURCE`, it is removed in getRedfishArgr function of the sdbusplus also.

I was curious where the version was coming from here and realized you're using the wrong version in sdbusplus.  I don't know how to make this work with your proposal.  Only bmcweb has the proper redfish message id version.
The bmcweb is not needing the version information while parsing Redfish logs (Only need the Registries prefix and event name)
Please elaborate.  How do we know the Redfish event matches the version in the message registry then?

In the bmcweb, it parses Redfish Message Id into 4 arguments `RegistryName.MajorVersion.MinorVersion.MessageKey`, based on the `RegistryName` and `MessageKey`, the bmcweb get the message registry, it does not use `MajorVersion` and `MinorVersion`.
Please refer to https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/redfish-core/src/registries.cpp#L70 for more detail.

But when bmcweb fills out the "MessageId" field in the response, it uses the raw messageID from the REDFISH_MESSAGE_ID.  The way you are filling this in, the message ID won't even be close to the correct Redfish version.

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/b360d5b91cff2c98113e259203a02e5e7d6963a2/redfish-core/lib/systems_logservices_journal_eventlog.hpp#L198

if you want to show the correct the version, I think we can update the version of events.yaml file in PDIs based on the version in the bmcweb.
E.g: In the bmcweb, the version of `sensor events` is `1.0.1` https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/scripts/parse_registries.py#L710, but the PDIs is defining the version of `sensor events` is `1.2.0` https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Sensor/Threshold.events.yaml#L1. We should update the `version` in the `Threshold.events.yaml` to `1.0.1`

No, the PDI files are _not_ Redfish files.  They have their own versioning directives.  This is what I keep saying is a fundamental gap.  There isn't enough information to do what you want to do, so why not just implement it properly in bmcweb?
Thank you for your information, I think we have to update bmcweb to replace the _version_ in the message Id with the correct defined _version_ in Redfish. Is this solution ok with you?
I'd prefer we just do the entire thing in bmcweb like I originally suggested but ... whatever you want to try to make work that isn't wrong and you can get consensus on.

Sorry for my misunderstanding. I created a new bmcweb commit (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/84496) to correct the version of MessageId. This issue appeared on the bmcweb, therefore, I don't add that commit to this Topic.
@patrick@stwcx.xyz Does this resolve your concern?
I've given my feedback that I'd prefer it done another way, but if you and @ed@tanous.net are ok with this direction then I am also ok with it.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/84453

My original design, which is implemented everywhere except bmcweb, is that phosphor-logging emits OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID journal entries (instead of the existing REDFISH_MESSAGE_ID one).  The transformation of these can be done in bmcweb, just like we have pending commits to do the transformation from the phosphor-logging objects.

What this topic from @thuutran@amperecomputing.com is doing is to have us emit old-style REDFISH_MESSAGE_IDs (which isn't entirely accurate because we're still having to do fix-ups in bmcweb) and spread the transformation out between sdbusplus/phosphor-logging/bmcweb.
Thank you for your answer @patrick@stwcx.xyz. You can find out more information at https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/867820390406422538/1424948698269614131 @spinler@us.ibm.com

In that chat you said this:

> The OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID record has a dynamic structure (following JSON format), which makes it difficult to filter messages using rsyslog.

Can you elaborate on this?  Why would we be doing filtering?  Can't we match on the OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID and put the whole content into the redfish log file?

The `/var/log/redfish` file is storing Redfish events that follow format `<Timespame> <RedfishMessageId><RedfishMessageArguments>`. Currently, rsyslog filters structured journal logs that have the keys `REDFISH_MESSAGE_ID` and `REDFISH_MESSAGE_ARGS` then store to `/var/log/redfish` file (You can refer to this example https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/47982c492d22f2cd4bbb429676c6a2ef0236f291/meta-evb/meta-evb-arm/meta-evb-fvp-base/recipes-extended/rsyslog/rsyslog/rsyslog.conf#L41). However, the `OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID` record does not have `RedfishMessageId`. Instead, it contains many keys that correspond to argument names, which makes parsing `RedfishMessageArguments` difficult.

If we want to store whole OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID record then we have to update rsyslog configuration files of platforms to filter OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID records. This will result in two different Redfish log formats in the same file, making the content messy. Additionally, bmcweb will need to be updated to parse both formats in `/var/log/redfish`,  which would require unnecessary extra effort.
Sorry for this late response, I forgot to press the `Send` button 😞

I don't see anything insurmountable here.  There is nothing fixed in stone about the format currently in /var/log/redfish, is there?

> This will result in two different Redfish log formats in the same file, making the content messy. 

This really isn't hard.  Have new messages prefix with `OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID` instead of the RedfishMessageId.  Then you know if it is the new-style or the old style.

> Additionally, bmcweb will need to be updated to parse both formats in /var/log/redfish, which would require unnecessary extra effort.

Additional work is not, to me, a reason to spread details across 3 repositories.

> I don't see anything insurmountable here.  There is nothing fixed in stone about the format currently in /var/log/redfish, is there?
> This really isn't hard.  Have new messages prefix with `OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID` instead of the RedfishMessageId.  Then you know if it is the new-style or the old style.

IMO, the format of a data file should be consistent, we should not mix 2 formats.

> Additional work is not, to me, a reason to spread details across 3 repositories.

This is a solution to avoid missing Redfish events during transitional period. When all applications have switched to using lg2::commit to log events to D-Bus object paths, I believe we can remove this solution. Therefore, spending so much effort parsing both formats in the /var/log/redfish file is not a good choice.

@ed@tanous.net, Could you share your thoughts on mixing two event formats in the /var/log/redfish file and whether bmcweb must support both formats?
@spinler@us.ibm.com, Do you have any comments for my solution?
I wouldn't mind hearing Ed's opinion.

Version-wise, I really don't care.  It's "technically" a breaking Redfish API change to move the version from 0.1 to 0.5.  Every Redfish client implementation I know of completely ignores the version field when parsing real events, and the compliance tools only verify that the version exists in the registry the instance publishes.  That seems fair if we want to start publishing "only the latest" version of each message.  FWIW, we've treated the schemas themselves that way for forever, so it's somewhat expected that version doesn't matter so long as you ignore keys you don't understand.

I've +1ed the bmcweb review itself.  I didn't +2 in case this group has more comments or thinks this is ill advised.

> I'd prefer we just do the entire thing in bmcweb like I originally suggested

I'm not sure I understand the difference here.  I think the latest patchset was everything being done in bmcweb?  Or are you saying we should omit the versions entirely in this file?


> Therefore, spending so much effort parsing both formats

I don't care much if we want to parse both formats, so long as there's a way to correctly parse both formats from a single set of code (arg number differences or something to determine the difference?).  I'm not sure I understand the other format being proposed, but so long as both end up with a correct version, MessageId, Message, and Args in the Redfish https response (which is what users and compliance tools care about) I'm fine with whatever code needs to exist to make that happen.  Where I'll get worried is if we claim to need to functionally break the user-facing behavior that's working correctly for the sake of cleaner code.

The new Redfish message format can be `<Timestamp> OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID,<Whole Message>`.
- <Timestamp>: The time Redfish event is stored.
- OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID: Prefix to indicate the new format.
- <Whole Message>: Message data in json format. {<EventName>:{<Args Name>:<Args Value>: "_SOURCE":{"COLUMN":<>, "FILE":<>,"FUNCTION":<>,"LINE":<>,"PID":<>}}}

E.g: When users use log-create CLI to create an Ampere Event: 
```
log-create com.ampere.Event.ReportedSEL.ReportedSELCritical -j \
'{"SOURCE": "Test Source", "MESSAGE": "Test Message", "RAW_DATA": "Test Data"}'
```
this event shall be stored in the /var/log/redfish file as 
```
2025-11-06T16:05:47.129348+00:00 OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID,{"com.ampere.Event.ReportedSEL.ReportedSELCritical":{"MESSAGE":"Test Message","RAW_DATA":"Test Data","SOURCE":"Test Source","_SOURCE":{"COLUMN":45,"FILE":"../git/log_create_main.cpp","FUNCTION":"int generate_event(const std::string&, const nlohmann::json_abi_v3_12_0::json&)","LINE":34,"PID":12764}}}
```

@patrick@stwcx.xyz, please correct me if the new message format is wrong.

Do you have any comments about new format? 
Should we accept this format or create old format in lg2::commit method?
@patrick@stwcx.xyz, Do you have any comment about new Redfish message format?
@thuutran@amperecomputing.com - I am ok with your proposed /var/log/redfish format.

In the new record format, we have two tasks to parse this record into a Redfish message:
1. Map `EventName` to `Redfish Message ID`.
2. Parse Argruments's values.

I noticed that in the patch https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/78481/18, it is trying to do 2 above tasks (data from Dbus object path). However, it seems this patch is no longer maintained by its owner. We will need to add some similar patches to convert data from record to Redfish message, which could make some implicit issues in bmcweb.

In my solution, it made small changes to the sdbusplus and phosphor-logging,making it easier to review. Additionally, we don't have to update the `rsyslog.conf` files in platfroms to collect `OPENBMC_MESSAGE_ID` records. IMO, my solution is better suited to prevent missing Redfish events during the transitional period as we move to using lg2::commit method to log Redfish events.

That is from another Meta developer, who is I think waiting on an earlier commit of mine in the stack to be cleaned up so it can be merged.  Ideally you would build upon this work.
If we _were_ going to go this route, we should just get rid of this path and option, right?
I want to keep it as your design https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/event-logging.md#phosphor-logging. Beside that, I add `none` value to the `lg2_commit_strategy` option.
But why?  If nobody is going to use this other path, let's get rid of it.  It's pretty trivial to update the design document accordingly, isn't it?  Design documents aren't etched in stone.
I updated `LG2_COMMIT_JOURNAL` to generate `REDFISH_MESSAGE_ID` instead. Additional, I updated `event-logging` design at https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/84453

I haven't read this whole review, but the problem has always been that each Redfish logging mechanism supported different features.  MessageId, Eventing, mutable Resolved field, >1000 event storage limit performance, and Redfish registries are the 5 major differences that I knew of.  Any answer I give to "do we need both" would need to be rooted in someones (maybe mine, maybe not mine) analysis of the features of each, and understand if we're dropping any functionality.  If we're truly not dropping anything, and we have refactoring patches in place to move one implementation to the other, I'm fine here, but every time I've looked, each mechanism supported different features.   There's been people trying to close that gap, which is great!
